items.title: Pay alleged import duties/customs handling fee
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar due date (09.11.2026) rather than a period to be counted, so that printed date is used directly as the due date. No delivery-fiction or period-counting rules apply since the date is given as a fixed calendar date.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a parcel/customs scam: genuine German customs (Zoll) never demands payment for import duties via a private company's bank account, only through official assessment notices with a Steuernummer/Abgabenbescheid and payment to a public treasury account (Bundeskasse), not to a company called 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.'
The payee IBAN (DE96 7001 0080 0661 2345 67) is held by a private company name unrelated to any German customs authority – a classic sign of payment-redirection fraud; do not transfer money to it.

The letter insists on contact 'ausschließlich per WhatsApp' (exclusively via WhatsApp) and lists a generic mobile number, which is not how German authorities or legitimate parcel/customs services communicate – this is a common scam pattern to avoid traceable channels.

The sender's email domain 'clearance-mail.example' and the generic 'Musterstadt/Frachtweg 1/44147 Musterstadt' address (note: 'Musterstadt' is literally German for 'sample/example town') are placeholder-style and not identifiable as a real, verifiable company or authority.

A very short 4-day payment deadline combined with a threat to destroy or return the parcel is a pressure tactic typical of fraudulent collection letters; verify independently with the actual shipping carrier or German customs (Zoll) before paying anything.

No legal remedy instructions (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) are given at all, which would be unusual for a genuine official customs assessment (Einfuhrabgabenbescheid), further suggesting this is not an authentic government notice.
